entries.description: CI, release workflow, and release handoff now reference the lowercase Linux aether artifact; GoReleaser config, generated artifact names, focused provider diagnostic redaction tests, and TypeScript host typecheck passed. No release blocker found in the targeted final verification.
Phase 5 runtime verification records go build, go vet, and go test ./... passing; seal review also reran go test ./... -race successfully.
entries.suggestion: Keep full local smoke output attached to verification artifacts for future seals.

entries.description: Focused Go tests cover hosted execution stderr redaction and debug artifact redaction with sk-proj, ghp, token, prompt, stdout, stderr, and parse-error secret fixtures.
entries.suggestion: Keep these tests in the release gate because they directly cover the previous high-risk leak path.

entries.description: Real invoker failure coverage verifies RawOutput and error strings do not leak provider stdout/stderr secrets.
entries.suggestion: Keep fake-provider failure tests credential-free and deterministic.

entries.description: TS host sanitizer coverage proves failed-worker summary redaction for provider-like secrets; go-bridge tests also cover subprocess output and Go error-envelope redaction.
entries.suggestion: Add a higher-level TS dispatch failure test when the real-worker dispatch path becomes easier to inject or export.

entries.description: CI and release workflows reference the lowercase Linux aether artifact path; local Darwin snapshot binaries report the expected snapshot version. Direct Linux execution on Darwin is not a valid local smoke path.
entries.suggestion: Keep host-specific binary smoke instructions in the release handoff.

entries.description: The security ledger still lists the pre-implementation HIGH provider-output-redaction item as open even though later code and tests address it.
entries.suggestion: Mark superseded or resolved ledger entries, or attach evidence references, so future reviewers do not re-triage stale HIGH findings as active blockers.

entries.description: The phase continue review wave was skipped with --skip-watchers; this seal review compensates, but the phase report alone lacks final review-agent evidence.
entries.suggestion: When skip-watchers is used, attach seal-review outputs or a deterministic review substitute to the phase evidence bundle.

entries.description: Core verification JSON records build, vet, and go test, but not the full phase smoke list such as race, GoReleaser snapshot build, npm typecheck/test/build, and binary smoke; those are currently distributed across worker summaries and handoff notes.
entries.suggestion: Promote full smoke command outputs into verification.json or a command evidence ledger for seal-time review.

entries.description: Proceed with seal from the Probe perspective; no blocker-level missing coverage or red verification evidence remains.
Record full smoke commands as structured evidence in future final phases, especially race, GoReleaser snapshot build, npm TS-host commands, and binary smoke.
Resolve or supersede stale HIGH/MEDIUM security-ledger entries after finalizer acceptance so future release reviews start from the current risk state.
Linux artifact path can be checked on Darwin, but executing that Linux binary locally fails by platform design; local binary smoke must use the matching Darwin artifact.
entries.suggestion: Add focused coverage before expanding the sealed surface.

entries.description: Machine-readable phase verification is narrower than the handoff smoke list; seal review filled the race and focused redaction gaps, but future reviewers should not need to reconstruct this from worker summaries.
entries.suggestion: Add focused coverage before expanding the sealed surface.

entries.description: TS host failed-worker summary redaction has direct sanitizer coverage and code inspection evidence, but not a higher-level real-worker dispatch failure regression test.

entries.description: A skipped phase review wave shifts evidence burden to deterministic verification and seal-review workers.
Post-launch worker stderr/stdout containing sk-proj, ghp, token, prompt, stdout, stderr, and parse-error secrets must be redacted in errors, RawOutput, and debug JSON.
Release binary smoke is case-sensitive on Linux; workflows must reference dist/Aether_linux_amd64_v1/aether, not an uppercase binary name.
Worker-debug artifacts should preserve byte counts while sanitizing prompt args and stdout/stderr excerpts.
